notes.decision: 'Deceits' — Lyc. ⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ = Sah. ϭⲗⲟⲡⲉ 'deceit, secret thing'. Plural here designates the three cosmic deceits (water/darkness/fire) hidden in the bodies of the archons. Continues from previous page.
'Stricken/afflicted' — qualitative or relative form, root unclear. Possibly from ϩⲱⲱⲥ/ϩⲱϣ 'afflict' or related to ⲥⲱⲡ/ⲥⲱⲡⲥⲡ 'wounded.' Context (man with disease) is unambiguous.
Greek loanword πληγή 'blow, wound, plague' — the dotted variants are scribal. Pairs with ⲓⲁⲃⲉ/ϣⲱⲛⲉ as the bodily afflictions the physician treats.
'Other poisons' — ⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'poison, venom' (Crum 192b) with ⲕⲉ- prefix and -ⲟⲩ plural. Pairs with χολή 'gall' as toxic humors in the diseased body.
Greek loanword εὐκαιρία 'good occasion, opportune moment' — the medical timing for treatment.

'(He) finds' — recurring verb opening each new medicine in the parable (lines 5, 6, 7). Lycopolitan verb form of uncertain root, possibly contracted from ϩⲏⲧ + ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ ('elect with mind') or ⲛⲏϫ 'apply.' Translated 'find' on contextual parallelism with the parable's three medicaments.
'Out against the taste' — antidote works against the bitter taste/savor of the disease. ⲧⲡⲧⲉ = ⲧⲡⲉ 'taste' (already in glossary).
'Purgative' — agent-noun ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who') + ϣⲟⲩⲟ ('pour out'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' Names a medicine that purges/evacuates the lower body's disease.
'To soothe' — ⲗⲁⲅⲉ likely from ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄ 'soft, sweet' or ⲗⲱⲕⲍ 'sweeten' — fits soothing medicine for blows/wounds. ⲛ̄- here functions as infinitive marker.
'The Living Spirit himself' — ⲍⲱϩ = Lyc. reflexive ϩⲱⲱϥ, intensifying the subject. Standard Manichaean cosmological figure (third member of the second emanation).
'The healing' — verbal noun from ⲧⲁⲗϭⲟ 'heal, cure.' The three garments are 'medicines of the healing' worn by the Living Spirit upon his cosmic body.

'That of the wind, that of the water, with that of the fire' — the three garments of the Living Spirit (cf. K.39 'three garments'). Note that ⲡⲙⲁⲩ here is 'water' (= ⲙⲟⲟⲩ); contrasts with the deceits-triplet (water/darkness/fire) where ⲙⲁⲩ also = water. The dark-water deceit is countered by the wind-garment, the dark-darkness deceit by the water-garment, the dark-fire deceit by the fire-garment.
'Single-mindedness' — already in glossary; the Living Spirit's unified manifestation in revealing himself to the upper archons.

'An expulsion forth' — ϣⲛϣ root unclear; possibly Lyc. ϣⲱⲛⲥ 'plunder, ravage' or ϣⲛ̄ϣ̄ 'service.' Context (revealing self forth, then pouring out the three deceits) suggests an expulsive/cleansing action. Tentative; flagging for parallels.

'The marrow' — literally ⲡⲁⲧ-ⲕⲉⲥ 'that-of-the-bone,' i.e. the substance within the bone. First (innermost) of the seven body-layers in the womb-child schema. Sequence: marrow → bone → sinew → flesh → vein → bond → skin.

'The bond' — sixth in the seven-part body series. Already in glossary as 'bond, fetter,' but here in anatomical register it likely names ligament/connective tissue (that-which-binds-together). Maintained as 'bond' for terminological consistency.
'The other garment' — ⲕⲉ- 'other' + ⲍⲃⲥ 'garment' (= ϩⲃⲥⲱ). The womb-child's body itself is one garment; the actual cloth garments after birth are the 'other garment.'
